description: Phase 3B runner exit-management test on all 15 Phase 3A favorites. Runner is activated by base/5m ADX(14)+DI alignment at thresholds 40 or 45. No break-even and no protected mode; initial TP is disabled only after runner activation, then runtime exits are RSI 5m and/or EMA100/200 cross.
notes: ADX runner activation is the old mechanism: timeframe='base' (5m), period=14, adx_threshold 40 or 45, require_di_alignment=true.
No break-even stop management is enabled.
No protected phase is used. phase_rules jump directly to runner.
Stop management remains empty in every managed candidate.
At runner activation the initial TP is disabled via take_profile_switch; stop loss remains the original initial SL.
Runtime exits: RSI 5m p14 85/15, RSI 5m p14 90/10, EMA100/200 cross, and RSI+EMA combinations.
All 15 Phase 3A favorite branches are preserved; do not collapse them into one winner before analysis by class.

favorites.note: original Phase 2D candidate after proper high-RR 1h TP

exit_profiles.purpose: diagnostic control: disables initial TP after runner but provides no new runtime exit

runtime_exits: EMA100/200 cross loss exit on base timeframe

main_candidate_should: improve or preserve PF without destroying long/short PF symmetry
improve high-MFE capture/giveback diagnostics if available
not rely only on performance-only branches
be analyzed separately by branch class: historical, current symmetric, high-sample relaxed, 1h-width, performance-only
reject_as_main_if: initial TP disable creates huge giveback without compensating PF/PnL
performance-only branch dominates raw PnL but clean/high-sample branches degrade
